{"basis":"measured","confidence":1.0,"fact_type":"defect","name":"A test was made to pass locally by adding the feature flag its failure named — which turned the CI contract into a workaround and failed the core job","statement":"OBSERVED 2026-09-07, on the agent, in the same session as two other instances of the same class.

WHAT HAPPENED. A new core test called search_design and reindex_search. Run locally it failed with a precise, well-written refusal: "this reflow2 was built without the `fulltext` feature, so there is no search index to rebuild". The agent added `--features fulltext` to its own command line, saw green, ran the WORKSPACE suite (which builds with the feature), saw green again, and pushed. CI's core job runs `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` and failed on all three tests.

THE MISREADING, precisely: the refusal was read as a fact about the local command line rather than as a fact about a SHIPPED CONFIGURATION. It says the binary was built without a feature - which is exactly what one CI job does on purpose, to prove the core works with no search index and no RocksDB. The flag that made it pass locally is the flag that job does not pass.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE HABIT IN ONE SESSION, and the pattern is worth more than any of them: (1) the sequence-hint fix landed in add_epoch and not its sibling plan_epoch; (2) the reachability map covered the tools named add_* and not the setters that leak the same way; (3) this. Each time the fix was correct where it was applied and the same question was never asked one step over. The project's own memory names it - A SUBSET OF A GATE SET IS NOT THE GATE SET - with a measurement beside it: `-p reflow2-core` plus `-p reflow2-mcp` run separately is 1778 tests against `--workspace`'s 1824, forty-six short, because a workspace build unifies the rocksdb feature onto core. That note was written for exactly this and was not read.

THE PROPER FIX, and it is not the obvious one. The obvious fix is to gate the whole test file behind the fulltext feature, which makes CI green and DELETES the coverage from the job that has no index. Instead the test was split: `claim_age_of` needs no index at all - it reads a property bag and one incoming edge - so the shared computation is tested in EVERY job, and only the two assertions that genuinely require a search surface are gated. The half that can be checked everywhere now is.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other tests would fail under `--no-default-features` if written today. No sweep was run; the local habit of reaching for the feature flag is what needs changing, and the only evidence it has changed will be the next test that does not do it.","subject_id":"art:search","valid_from":"2026-09-07"}
